case_title: Polamuri Chandra Sekhararao @ Chinna @ Babji v. State of A.P.
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (nephew; son of the accused's elder sister)
evidence_type: Circumstantial evidence (eye-witnesses PWs-1 and 2 turned hostile); medical evidence; recovery of knife; forensic (FSL) report; relatives' testimony
confession: Alleged: at the police station the accused stated he had killed the deceased with the knife (prosecution case). Not separately decided as a confession; the accused's admissions under s.313 of certain facts were noted.
aggravating_circumstances: 17 injuries including 13 incised cut injuries; body found within accused's compound; accused gave no explanation for the body's presence
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302; life imprisonment and fine of Rs. 1,000 with three months simple imprisonment in default
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence upheld
neutral_facts: On an evening in April 2004, the victim rode a motorcycle to the accused's house, where the accused and his two adult daughters were chatting outside. The accused asked why the victim had come. The victim reportedly said he wished to marry both daughters and challenged the accused to say whom he would give them to in marriage. The accused allegedly became enraged, fetched a long knife from his bedroom and struck the victim several times. The victim collapsed and died. The victim's body was later found in the compound of the accused's house. The accused and the two daughters then went to a police station on a two-wheeler, and the accused handed over the knife, stating he had killed the victim. One daughter's statement was registered as a complaint. A technician witness was present when police seized the knife. Forensic examination found human blood on the knife, though the blood group could not be traced. The post-mortem recorded 17 injuries, 13 of them incised cuts, and the doctor said such cuts could have been caused by a knife of this kind. The two daughters, who were the main eyewitnesses, did not support the complaint when examined. Several relatives of the victim gave evidence. The accused was estranged from his wife, and the victim had been living in the same house as the wife and daughters. The accused admitted several of these background facts. The accused's version was that he had gone shopping with his daughters, but no supporting evidence was produced.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from hemorrhage and shock; multiple incised cut injuries including on the neck (17 injuries in total)
premeditation_planning: Not stated; the court found the killing followed anger at the victim's conduct, and no premeditation finding is made
motive: Accused was enraged by the victim's attempt to develop a close relationship with the accused's daughter (PW-2); the accused was also not on good terms with PW-3, the victim's mother
key_evidence_accepted: Dead body found in accused's compound (not disputed); report to police by PWs-1 and 2 along with accused (Ext. P-1); knife M.O.-10 seized under Ext. P-5; FSL report finding human blood on knife; doctor's evidence that incised injuries could be caused by the knife; accused's admissions
witness_credibility: Hostile PWs 1 and 2: their presence at the police station was admitted and the correctness of Ext. P-1 could not be questioned; their shopping alibi was rejected for lack of supporting evidence. Related witnesses PWs 3, 4, 6 and 7: relationship alone not a reason to disbelieve them.
post_offence_conduct: Accused went to the police station with his daughters and handed over the knife; accused did not explain how the body came to be in his premises
trial_duration: offence: 06.04.2004; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 28.03.2008; Supreme Court: 23.07.2012
legal_representation: Accused: Chanchal Kumar Ganguli. State: Amit K. Nain.
investigation_status: Complaint registered under IPC s.302 on 06.04.2004; knife seized; FSL report obtained; 15 witnesses examined; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302 IPC, life imprisonment. High Court: appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 646 of 2006) dismissed, 28.03.2008. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: PW-1 was hostile, so the trial court could rely on other circumstances; motive existed; the accused gave no proper explanation for the body in his courtyard; alibi not proved, so the conviction should stand
defence_argument: With PWs 1 and 2 hostile, Ext. P-1 could not be acted upon; the remaining witnesses (PWs 3, 4, 6, 7) were related to the deceased and not eyewitnesses, so their evidence could not be relied on; no incriminating circumstance connected the accused with the death
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence: the chain of circumstances must point to guilt; the accused's failure to explain the body's presence in his premises; hostile witnesses' contrary testimony may be assessed against other material; relationship with witnesses alone does not make their evidence unreliable
judicial_aggravating_factors: Brutal multiple knife wounds causing instantaneous death; body found in accused's premises with no explanation from the accused
